title: Per-customer Terraform extension pattern: tile modules, upgrade hooks, and rollout-aware health checks
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create and validate a maintainable pattern for per-customer Terraform customizations that avoids forking core modules. Key pieces: (1) 'tile' modules that act as composable extension points, (2) a safe upgrade hook mechanism that runs post-apply customer-side migrations or service restarts, and (3) rollout-aware health checks that integrate with canary/traffic-shift plans. Deliver a documented reference implementation (repo + example overlay) and CI gates that run health probes during upgrades.
acceptance_criteria: Reference implementation: a small repo with core modules + a customer tile module demonstrating config overrides and extension hooks
Upgrade hook mechanism implemented with Terraform patterns (null_resource / external) documented and tested in CI
Health check integration: synthetic probe job that can be triggered by release pipeline and influenced by canary weight
Migration considerations documented: idempotency, retry/backoff, and rollback signals
Security review completed for hook execution paths and credentials (KMS/SSM/HSM patterns)
comments: 2025-02-28 | Maya Chen: Kickoff - scoped to minimum viable pattern that avoids module forking. Strong requirement: customers must be able to inject VPC-specific resources (security groups, route tables) and small runtime actions without editing core modules.

2025-03-01 | Liam O'Neill: Prototype complete - introduced 'tile' module concept: core modules expose extension points via module outputs and input maps. Tile modules are independent Terraform modules placed under customers/<tenant>/tile-modules and composed by a small aggregator module in top-level root.

2025-03-02 | Priya Kapoor (SE): Reviewed prototype. Notes: prefer provider aliasing per-tenant to avoid global collisions. Suggested pattern for variable scoping: pass a 'tenant_context' object and restrict sensitive values to SSM/KMS references only.

2025-03-03 | Liam O'Neill: Spike for upgrade hooks - implemented two options: (A) terraform null_resource with local-exec that triggers a signed webhook to a customer's control-plane agent; (B) external provisioner that writes an SSM document to the instance which the agent picks up. Option A is simpler for hosted-managed nodes; option B required for air-gapped/on-prem. Chosen: implement both and document trade-offs.

2025-03-04 | Security (Daniel R.): Reviewed hook paths. Concern: null_resource local-exec with stored plain tokens is unacceptable. Action: switch to short-lived signed JWTs via KMS/HSM, rotate per-run, and make hook payload non-sensitive. Added requirement for audit events to be emitted.

2025-03-05 | QA (Aisha S.): Ran CI job that applies example customer overlay in a sandbox. Health check job executed post-apply; detected flaky probe under 95% load. Next action: add probe retry/exponential backoff and a 'safety hold' step in the pipeline where the canary remains at low weight until N successful checks.

2025-03-05 | Liam O'Neill: Pushed draft PR with README and examples. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2731. Requesting review from infra and security teams. Follow-ups: add docs page and small workshop with SEs to walk through pattern.

2025-03-05 | Maya Chen: Note for rollout plan - tie Terraform apply to release-operator pipeline that will: 1) run terraform plan, 2) apply to non-production sandbox, 3) run health probes, 4) trigger production apply with canary weights, 5) run sequential health checks and escalate on failures. Document rollback signal mapping (terraform destroy vs. application-level rollback).
